cleanIntro: This guide follows CZ's CZ DUTY instruction manual, which does not print "4.0", so check your pistol against it. The DUTY 4.0 MS carries a manual safety, and CZ's book covers it. The pistol strips without a trigger press: magazine out, slide locked open on the slide stop, the disassembling lever turned down to its end stop, the slide released forward and run off the grip. CZ's book also gives the owner the firing pin and the magazine to take apart after a higher number of rounds, and stops there.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows CZ's CZ DUTY instruction manual, which does not print "4.0", so check your pistol against it. This row is the DUTY 4.0 MS, the version fitted with a manual safety; note whether yours is also Optics Ready, Suppressor Ready or both.
steps.prose: CZ prints one book for the whole DUTY line and describes its versions in it. The strip below is the same for all of them. The book's Pistol Securing section, which covers the manual safety, applies to this pistol.
steps.quote: Some versions of the pistol can be fitted with a manual safety.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Description and Terminology, printed p.3

steps.title: Know your manual safety
steps.action: Find the safety fingergrip; it works from the right or the left side. Pushed up, it locks in a slanted position and the trigger cannot be pulled. Moved back to horizontal, the pistol is ready to fire.
steps.prose: CZ describes the safety as the way to secure a loaded pistol with the mechanism cocked. It is not a substitute for unloading: the magazine still comes out and the chamber is still checked in the next steps.
steps.quote: In this way, the firearm mechanism is secured and the trigger cannot be pulled.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Operating Instructions — Pistol Securing, printed p.7

steps.title: Magazine out before anything else
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Press the ambidextrous magazine catch and let the magazine fall out of the grip.
steps.prose: CZ makes this the first step of the strip and says plainly that the pistol must not be taken apart with a magazine in it. The magazine drops free when the catch is pressed, so keep a hand under the grip.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine. The pistol must not be disassembled with the magazine inserted
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 1, printed p.11

steps.title: Clear the chamber and look
steps.action: Draw the slide back and check that the cartridge in the chamber has been extracted and thrown clear. Look into the chamber before you go on.
steps.prose: CZ's unloading sequence is magazine out, slide back to extract and eject, slide forward, then an aimed safety shot into a safe area. The strip itself does not need that trigger press: CZ built the DUTY to come apart without operating the trigger.
steps.quote: Draw back the slide and verify the last cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Operating Instructions — Unloading the Pistol, printed p.8

steps.title: Lock the slide open on the slide stop
steps.action: Hold the pistol by the grip and push the slide stop fingergrip up with your thumb. With the other hand pull the slide fully back by its checkered part and release it carefully, so the slide stop holds it open.
steps.prose: The open slide is the starting position for the disassembling lever. With the magazine already out, use the thumb on the slide stop rather than an empty magazine to hold it back.
steps.quote: 2. Set the slide into the locked open position (on the slide stop) as it is described in the previous part of the manual.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, printed p.11

steps.title: Turn the disassembling lever down to its stop
steps.action: Turn the disassembling lever downwards until it reaches its end stop, about 100 degrees.
steps.prose: The lever only turns this far with the slide locked open. CZ notes that if the sequence is not done correctly the disassembling mechanism blocks, so a lever that will not move is a sign to go back a step, not to push harder.
steps.quote: 3. Turn the disassembling lever downwards up to the end stop
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 3, printed p.11

steps.title: Release the slide forward
steps.action: Hold the slide by its checkered part in one hand and the grip in the other. Push the slide stop fingergrip down and let the slide run to its front position under control.
steps.prose: Keep hold of the slide as it goes forward; it is still on the grip at this point and comes off in the next step.
steps.quote: 4. Grasp the slide by the checkered part with one hand. Use your other and to grasp the grip and push the slide stop fingergrip downwards, releasing the slide to its front position.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 4, printed p.11

steps.title: Slide off the front of the grip
steps.action: Shift the slide forward off the grip.
steps.prose: No trigger press is involved at any point. CZ lists safe disassembly without pulling the trigger among the DUTY's safety features.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the slide from the grip by shifting it forward.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 5, printed p.11

steps.title: Recoil springs out, then the barrel
steps.action: Turn the slide over. Lift out the set of recoil springs first, then the barrel.
steps.prose: The order is CZ's: the springs come out before the barrel. The recoil spring set is one assembly with a guide, an outer and an inner spring.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the set of recoil springs and, finally, the barrel from the slide
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, printed p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Grip, slide, barrel and recoil spring set, with the magazine set aside. That is CZ's strip for cleaning, done without touching the trigger.
steps.prose: These parts give access to the bore and chamber, the slide and the grip for cleaning. CZ's deeper owner work, the firing pin and the magazine, is in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: When disassembling the firearm, it is not necessary to operate the trigger.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Safety Features — Safe disassembling without pulling the trigger, printed p.6

steps.title: Bore and chamber with patches
steps.action: If the pistol has been fired little or not at all, run clean patches on a cleaning rod through the bore and chamber, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean.
steps.prose: For a very dirty bore, brush in a gun cleaning solution, let it act about ten minutes, scrub the bore, then dry the bore and chamber with a clean patch and check the fouling is gone.
steps.quote: Repeat the cleaning, changing patches, until the last patch comes out clean.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Cleaning the Barrel Bore and the Cartridge Chamber, printed p.12

steps.title: Rod and brush in from the chamber
steps.action: Put the rod and brush into the barrel from the chamber end. Push the brush all the way through before drawing it back.
steps.prose: CZ gives two reasons: entering from the chamber protects the muzzle, and a brush reversed inside the bore can stick.
steps.quote: The cleaning rod and the brush must be inserted into the barrel bore from the chamber, to prevent wear or damage to the muzzle.
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Cleaning the Barrel Bore and the Cartridge Chamber, printed p.12

steps.title: Other parts dry, never with bore cleaner
steps.action: Clean the slide, grip and the outside of the barrel with a dry cloth, an old toothbrush, a brass bristle brush or a wooden scraper. Preserving oil or paraffin oil can be used.
steps.prose: Keep the bore cleaning agent off these parts; CZ warns it can stay in the joints and cause corrosion later. Check that no cloth fibres or bristles are left behind.
steps.quote: Never use the agent designed for barrel bore cleaning!
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Cleaning of Other Pistol Parts, printed p.13

steps.title: Oil, then take the excess off
steps.action: With the bore, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or spray the oil on, then remove all excess oil.
steps.prose: Wipe the bore dry before shooting. In very low temperatures take the oil off the accessible parts or use a lubricant made for those conditions.
steps.quote: wipe these parts with a cloth soaked in gun oil or apply the oil in a spray. Remove all excess oil
steps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Preserving, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out of the slide
deepSteps.action: With the slide off the pistol, tilt the automatic firing pin safety away with your finger to its end position and push the firing pin forward.
deepSteps.prose: CZ advises cleaning the firing pin and its hole in the slide after a higher number of rounds, and gives the owner the procedure. Work over a bench; the parts are small.
deepSteps.quote: Use your finger to tilt away the automatic firing pin safety to its end position and push the firing pin forward.
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Firing Pin Disassembly, printed p.11

deepSteps.title: Slide the container forward out of the slide cover
deepSteps.action: Put a narrow tool into the hole in the firing pin container and shift the container forward until it slides out of the slide cover.
deepSteps.prose: Use a narrow tool that fits the hole without forcing it.
deepSteps.quote: Insert a narrow tool into the hole in the firing pin container and shift it forward, until it slides out of the slide cover (Fig. 8).
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Firing Pin Disassembly, printed p.11

deepSteps.title: Slide cover off, firing pin assembly out to the rear
deepSteps.action: Shift the slide cover out of the slide, then take the firing pin assembly out rearwards.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin assembly is the firing pin, its container, its spring and the two spring holders, per CZ's parts list.
deepSteps.quote: the slide cover out of the slide (Fig. 9), remove the firing pin assembly rearwards.
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Firing Pin Disassembly, printed p.11

deepSteps.title: Clean the firing pin parts and keep them dry
deepSteps.action: Clean the firing pin assembly, the firing pin hole in the slide and the related parts, or blow them clean with compressed air. Do not oil them.
deepSteps.prose: For use at very low temperatures CZ allows a very light coat of a low-temperature lubricant on the firing pin; otherwise these parts stay dry.
deepSteps.quote: Keep these parts dry, do not use common lubricants.
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Firing Pin Disassembly, printed p.11

deepSteps.title: Firing pin assembly back in reverse order
deepSteps.action: Refit the firing pin assembly in the reverse order. If the automatic safety pin moved out while you worked, push it back in with a narrow tool.
deepSteps.prose: Check that the automatic safety pin is home before the slide goes back on the pistol.
deepSteps.quote: Reassemble the firing pin assembly in the reverse order.
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Firing Pin Disassembly, printed p.11

deepSteps.title: Magazine base off, spring held
deepSteps.action: If the magazine base has a hole, push the base lock through it and slide the base slightly forward; if it has a sliding base lock at the rear, move it to the disassembly position and slide the base slightly forward. Cover the base with your thumb to hold the spring and slide the base out of its rails with the other hand.
deepSteps.prose: CZ warns the spring can fly out and cause an injury, so keep the magazine pointed away from your face and let the spring up slowly.
deepSteps.quote: There is a difference depending on the magazine design.
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — Magazine Disassembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: Stop there
deepSteps.action: Reassemble the magazine and go no further into the pistol. Anything that needs adjustment or repair goes to a competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.prose: This is where CZ's owner procedure ends.
deepSteps.quote: No further disassembly of your pistol is recommended.
deepSteps.cite: CZ DUTY — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (CZ's file name carries 07_2025) — Maintenance Instructions — CAUTION, printed p.12

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Patches on a rod through the bore and chamber until the last one comes out clean
Very dirty bore: brush in a gun cleaning solution, let it act about 10 minutes, scrub, then dry with a clean patch
Rod and brush go in from the chamber end, and the brush goes all the way through before it comes back
Never reverse the brush inside the bore

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BARREL & GRIP
tasks: Dry cloth, old toothbrush, brass bristle brush or wooden scraper on the slide, the grip and the outside of the barrel
Preserving oil or paraffin oil can be used for this cleaning
Never use the bore cleaning agent on these parts
Check that no cloth fibres or brush bristles are left in the pistol

cleaning.name: OIL & WIPE DOWN
tasks: Wipe the clean, dry bore, chamber and accessible parts with gun oil, or spray it on
In very low temperatures remove the oil or use a lubricant made for the cold
Wipe the bore dry before shooting

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, then the set of recoil springs.
Check that the disassembling lever is still turned down to its disassembly position, about 100 degrees.
Run the slide onto the grip from the front, take it to its rearmost position and set it on the slide stop.
Only then turn the disassembling lever back to horizontal.
If the lever was turned to horizontal before the slide was on the slide stop, push the lever out from the right side, take the slide off and do the sequence again.
fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber empty. With an empty magazine inserted, pull the slide fully back: the follower should push the slide stop up and hold the slide open. Push the slide stop down and the slide should run fully forward. The disassembling lever should sit horizontal. Push the manual safety up and check it locks in its slanted position, then return it to horizontal; it works from either side. If your DUTY is Suppressor Ready and no suppressor is fitted, cover the thread and muzzle with the muzzle cap, as CZ asks.
